note: Quick questions of the Cyber box. They are practice only: they never enter the decision ledger or the knowledge score. The first option is the right one; the game shuffles the order.

questions.qAr: What is a rumour?
questions.whyAr: It spreads fast when people pass it on unchecked.

questions.qAr: Big news with no writer or source. What do you ask first?
questions.whyAr: News with an unknown source can't be trusted.

questions.qAr: A friend sends news and writes "as received". Do you forward it?
options: No, not until I check it
questions.whyAr: If you pass on a rumour, you share in its harm.

questions.qAr: Photo: a shark swims in a wadi after rain! Your view?
options: Maybe edited; I find the original
questions.whyAr: Editing photos is easy. A photo alone is no proof.

questions.qAr: A clip of a famous player saying odd things, lips not matching his voice…
options: It may be made by AI
questions.whyAr: AI can copy faces and voices very well.

questions.qAr: An old wadi flood photo is posted as "now". How do you spot it?
options: I look for its first post date
questions.whyAr: Many old photos get posted again as if new.

questions.qAr: Clip title: "You won't believe what happened at school!" It is…
options: Bait for views, so I slow down
questions.whyAr: Exciting titles want your tap, not to help you.

questions.qAr: Classmates share a screenshot of an "official decision". Is it proof?
options: No, screenshots are easy to fake
Yes, if many people sent it
questions.whyAr: Anyone can change the words inside a picture.

questions.qAr: News worries you. Is it true? Who do you ask?
questions.whyAr: People you trust calm you and explain the truth.

questions.qAr: Two accounts use a government name. Which one is real?
questions.whyAr: Fakers make accounts that look like official ones.

questions.qAr: A viral clip mocks respect for parents. Your view?
options: Not our values, so I skip it
Funny; I copy it at home
questions.whyAr: A viral clip can't change our family values.

questions.qAr: Classmates ask you to try a risky viral challenge. What do you do?
options: I refuse and tell an adult
I try it so they don't mock me
I film it and post it
questions.whyAr: Your safety beats any trend. Brave kids say no.

questions.qAr: What is the "Not interested" button for?
questions.whyAr: It teaches the app what you don't want to see.

questions.qAr: You watched many prank clips today. What will the app show tomorrow?
options: More pranks; it follows what I watch
questions.whyAr: The algorithm repeats what you watch most.

questions.qAr: You dislike a classmate's clip. Your comment?
options: I write mean words under a fake name
questions.whyAr: Our manners online match those in the majlis.

questions.qAr: A classmate says: "Arabic is old. Write in another language." You say?
options: I mock Arabic for a laugh
questions.whyAr: Our language is who we are. New ones don't erase it.

questions.qAr: An account mocks our dress and customs to get views. What do you do?
options: I don't react, and I report it
I share its clip so all see it
questions.whyAr: Any reaction, even anger, spreads it more.

questions.qAr: You scrolled clips for 2 hours and lost track. What do you do?
options: I stop and set a screen limit
I hide it under my pillow
questions.whyAr: Short clips are built to keep you watching.

questions.qAr: A clip made you doubt one of our customs. What do you do?
options: I ask strangers in the comments
questions.whyAr: Your family lovingly explains the clip.

questions.qAr: A game rated 18+ is played by all your class. What do you do?
options: I pick a game for my age
I play it at a friend's
questions.whyAr: Age ratings protect you. They don't punish you.

questions.qAr: What's a "digital footprint"?
options: All I leave about me online
questions.whyAr: Your posts, comments and searches show who you are.

questions.qAr: Which of these is "personal data"?
questions.whyAr: Personal data points to you, so guard it.

questions.qAr: An app shows all followers your live location. What do you do?
options: I leave it on for them
I turn it on only at school
questions.whyAr: Live location is for family only, not everyone.

questions.qAr: You'll post a photo by the family car. What do you hide first?
questions.whyAr: The plate and house number point to your family.

questions.qAr: Your family is in Salalah for khareef. When to post photos?
options: Before we go, with our dates
questions.whyAr: Trip posts tell all that the house is empty.

questions.qAr: You snapped friends at the pitch. Do you tag their accounts?
options: I tag them and add their school
questions.whyAr: A tag ties the photo to their accounts in public.

questions.qAr: Your account is "public". What is best?
questions.whyAr: Privacy settings set who sees your photos and news.

questions.qAr: A "Which player are you?" quiz asks your name, birthday, phone…
options: I skip it; it takes my data
I fill it in to see
questions.whyAr: "Free" fun may cost you your data.

questions.qAr: You post a comment and delete it a minute later. Is it gone?
questions.whyAr: The internet remembers. Think, then post.

questions.qAr: You have a funny photo of your little brother asleep. Post it?
options: Not without his and my parents' OK
questions.whyAr: His photo is a trust. It may shame him later.

questions.qAr: An unknown player says he's your age, from your town. Believe him?
options: Yes, his photo is a child
questions.whyAr: Behind a screen, anyone can claim anything.

questions.qAr: A chat user says: "Don't tell your family we talk." What do you do?
options: I keep it; he trusts me
I ask why and keep chatting
questions.whyAr: Anyone hiding chats from your family means no good.

questions.qAr: A strange player says: "Let's chat in a private app." What do you do?
options: I agree; the game is crowded
I give him my phone number
questions.whyAr: Private apps are far from the eyes of the game and family.

questions.qAr: A stranger offers a rare "skin" as a free gift. What do you do?
options: I refuse; the gift may be bait
I take it and do as he asks
questions.whyAr: Strangers use gifts to win your trust.

questions.qAr: A classmate insults you in the class group. What do you do?
options: No insults back; I tell an adult
questions.whyAr: Insults back grow the problem, not fix it.

questions.qAr: You keep getting bullying messages. What do you do before blocking?
options: I delete them all to forget
questions.whyAr: Proof helps your family and school stop the bully.

questions.qAr: All mock a classmate's photo in the group. What do you do?
options: I back him and don't join in
I laugh too, so I'm not next
I send the photo to other groups
questions.whyAr: One kind word can change a bullied child's day.

questions.qAr: An account in your top player's name offers a signed shirt…
options: Likely fake; I ignore and report
I send my address for the shirt
questions.whyAr: Stars don't message fans to ask for their details.

questions.qAr: A friend's account asks for an "urgent" top-up card. What do you do?
options: I call to check it's him
I send the card at once
I take Mum's card in secret
questions.whyAr: The account may be stolen and posing as him.

questions.qAr: A game friend invites you to meet at the mall, just the two of you…
options: I go with a friend my age
questions.whyAr: Never meet a screen-only friend without your family.

questions.qAr: Dozens of new accounts repeat one sentence under a post. What are they?
questions.whyAr: Planned repeating makes you think everyone agrees.

questions.qAr: A post has 100,000 likes. Does that make it true?
options: Yes, if it has a picture
questions.whyAr: Likes can be bought. Truth isn't counted in likes.

questions.qAr: A group's posts all stir up anger between people. What do you do?
options: I leave; I share none of it
I join in and get angry too
questions.whyAr: Stirred anger makes you share without thinking.

questions.qAr: A post makes you furious. What do you do before commenting?
questions.whyAr: An angry comment stays, and you may regret it.

questions.qAr: A big storm is coming. Where do you get instructions?
questions.whyAr: Rumours grow in emergencies. Official sources are safest.

questions.qAr: A café has two Wi-Fi names that look alike. Which do you join?
options: I ask the staff which is right
questions.whyAr: A trickster may copy the name to watch you.

questions.qAr: A wall sticker: "Scan the code and win a phone." What do you do?
options: I send a photo to the group
questions.whyAr: The code hides where it will take you.

questions.qAr: You find a USB stick in the school yard. What do you do?
options: I hand it in and don't try it
I try it on our home PC
I try it on a school computer
questions.whyAr: It may be left on purpose to harm your device.

questions.qAr: An AI chatbot helps with homework. What do you never type in?
options: My full name, address and photos
A maths question I didn't get
questions.whyAr: What you tell a bot may be saved. Keep secrets out.

questions.qAr: On National Day you want to post something. What is best?
options: A true fact and a kind word
questions.whyAr: Good digital citizens spread truth and kindness.

call.sayAr: Hello! Breaking news: schools are closed tomorrow! Send it to all your groups now, before everyone else!

questions.qAr: What do you do?
options: Send it to every group right away
Post it in my status for everyone
questions.whyAr: True news is announced by the official source, not by an unknown caller.

call.sayAr: Hi! I have a shocking clip about a famous person. I will send it to you. Share it fast, before it gets deleted!

questions.qAr: What do you do?
options: Share it fast before it is deleted
Send it to my friends only
questions.whyAr: "Share it before it is deleted" is a trick to make you share without thinking.

call.sayAr: Hey! Join our new challenge: film yourself making fun of our clothes and customs, and win lots of followers!

questions.qAr: What do you do?
options: Refuse: our customs are not a joke
Join in to get more followers
Film it and delete it later
questions.whyAr: Whoever pushes you to mock your own customs does not wish you well.

call.sayAr: Hello! We will send you gifts if you post our clips on your account. Do not ask what is in them. Just post!

questions.qAr: What do you do?
questions.whyAr: Never post what you have not seen: your account carries your name and your values.

call.sayAr: Congratulations! You won a prize! Just tell me: what is your full name? Where do you live? Which school do you go to?

questions.qAr: What do you do?
options: Give nothing and end the call
Tell him so I get the prize
questions.whyAr: Name, home and school point to you: never give them to an unknown caller.

call.sayAr: Hello! I am doing research for the school. Send me a photo of your house from outside, and your location on the map.

questions.qAr: What do you do?
options: Refuse: where we live is private
Send the photo and the location
Send the location, not the photo
questions.whyAr: A photo of your house and its location show strangers where you are.

call.sayAr: I am your friend from the game! Let us meet today, just the two of us. And do not tell anyone in your family. Deal?

questions.qAr: What do you do?
options: Refuse, and tell my parents at once
Go and take my friend along
questions.whyAr: Anyone who asks you to keep a secret from your family is a danger: tell them at once.

call.sayAr: Hello, it is me! Do you not know my voice? I changed my number. Send me a photo of your father's card, quickly!

questions.qAr: What do you do?
options: Call my relative on the number I know
Send it: I know that voice
Send it, then tell my father
questions.whyAr: Voices can be copied today: check through the number you already know.

call.sayAr: Join our secret group now! It has news you will not find anywhere else. And add all your friends with you!

questions.qAr: What do you do?
options: Do not join, and block the number
Join alone to see what is in it
questions.whyAr: Unknown groups are a door for rumours and influence campaigns.

call.sayAr: The situation is very dangerous! Do not believe the official channels. Believe only me, and spread my words to everyone!

questions.qAr: What do you do?
options: Trust the official source; spread nothing
Believe him and spread his words
Wait, then share it if it is repeated
questions.whyAr: In a crisis the official source is the reference, not an unknown caller.
